details: The U.S. Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep its federal funds target range steady at 3.75%-4.00% following its meeting this week, after a 25 basis point hike in September. Despite the anticipated pause, a hawkish stance for future rate hikes, particularly in December, remains in play due to persistent inflation and robust U.S. economic activity. Futures markets imply a low probability (around 9-10%) of a hike this week, but significantly higher odds (75-90%) for a December increase. Upcoming data, including September Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation and Q3 GDP, will be crucial in shaping the future rate outlook.
title: Federal Reserve Poised for Rate Pause Amid Inflation Concerns

details: Several central banks globally are either expected to hike rates or maintain a hawkish posture. The Bank of Canada is anticipated to raise rates by 25 basis points to 2.50% this week, citing concerns over broadening and persistent inflation. Similarly, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand is expected to deliver its third consecutive 25 basis point hike, bringing its policy rate to 3.00% due to above-target inflation and robust economic recovery. The European Central Bank and Bank of Japan are likely to keep rates steady but may signal potential future tightening amidst inflation risks.
title: Global Central Banks Signal Continued Tightening or Hawkish Stances

details: The global economy has demonstrated resilience despite various shocks, with global growth projected at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, partly fueled by an AI-driven investment boom. However, global headline inflation is expected to rise to 4.7% in 2026 before easing to 4.1% in 2027. In the U.S., September's Consumer Price Index (CPI-U) showed a 3.74% year-over-year increase, with core CPI-U at 2.56% and energy prices seeing a notable rise. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) warns of downside risks from escalating conflicts, potential re-evaluation of AI expectations, renewed trade tensions, and fiscal vulnerabilities.
title: Global Economy Shows Resilience, but Inflationary Pressures Persist

details: Bitcoin has fallen below the $80,000 mark, trading near $79,500, influenced by significant spot Bitcoin ETF outflows totaling approximately $773 million on October 22 and 23. The price decline triggered an estimated $820-$837 million in cryptocurrency futures liquidations, with leveraged long positions accounting for over 90%. Elevated oil prices, ongoing U.S. inflation, and uncertainty surrounding the Federal Reserve's upcoming decision are contributing to reduced demand for speculative assets. While XRP showed relative stability this week, its longer-term correlation with Bitcoin remains strong.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $80,000 Amid ETF Outflows and Macro Uncertainty
